item_name: High-Risk Drug Classes: Use and Indication — Antipsychotic (N0415A1 Is taking; N0415A2 Indication noted)

lookback_source.quote: N0415A1. Antipsychotic: Check if an antipsychotic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

lookback_notes: 7-day look-back period; if the resident has been in the facility less than 7 days, the window is since admission/entry or reentry. The manual uses "7-day look-back period" and "7-day observation period" interchangeably for this item (p. N-6, p. N-7). The exact method of counting days relative to the ARD is not stated on these pages.

coding_levels.label: Antipsychotic — Is taking
coding_levels.definition: Check if an antipsychotic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415A1. Antipsychotic: Check if an antipsychotic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

coding_levels.label: Antipsychotic — Indication noted
coding_levels.definition: Check if there is an indication noted for all antipsychotic medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415A2. Antipsychotic: Check if there is an indication noted for all antipsychotic medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

coding_levels.label: Not checked
coding_levels.definition: The item form provides check boxes for Column 1 (Is taking) and Column 2 (Indication noted); a box left unchecked indicates the condition was not met (e.g., in the manual's example N0415D2 Hypnotic = not checked because indication for use was not noted).

source.quote: N0415D2. Hypnotic = not checked; indication for use of temazepam was not noted.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Check N0415A1 if an antipsychotic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415A1. Antipsychotic: Check if an antipsychotic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Check N0415A2 only if there is an indication noted for ALL antipsychotic medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415A2. Antipsychotic: Check if there is an indication noted for all antipsychotic medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Column 2 (Indication noted) is completed only when Column 1 is checked.

source.quote: Column 2: If Column 1 is checked, check if there is an indication noted for all medications in the drug class.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

source.quote: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used (e.g., oxazepam prescribed as a hypnotic is coded as an antianxiety medication).

source.quote: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Medications with more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification must be coded in all assigned categories/classifications regardless of how used; e.g., prochlorperazine, dually classified as an antipsychotic and an antiemetic, is coded as an antipsychotic.

source.quote: Medications that have more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification should be coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how it is being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Combination medications are coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination; e.g., a single tablet combining an antipsychotic and an antidepressant is coded in both the antipsychotic and antidepressant categories.

source.quote: Combination medications should be coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Include medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

source.quote: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

source.quote: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Count long-acting medications, such as fluphenazine decanoate or haloperidol decanoate, that are given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Count long-acting medications, such as fluphenazine decanoate or haloperidol decanoate, that are given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: For transdermal patches, capture the medication only if the patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

source.quote: To code N0415, only capture the medication if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Herbal and alternative medicine products (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root) are dietary supplements and should not be counted as medications.

source.quote: Therefore, they should not be counted as medications (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Column 1 is checked based on medications the resident is taking by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Column 1: Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Check N0415Z1, None of the above, if none of the listed medications (including antipsychotics) were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415Z1. None of the above: Check if none of the medications above were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal.criterion: Medical record documentation that the antipsychotic medication was received by the resident and documentation of the indication for its use during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal.notes: Step 1 of Steps for Assessment for N0415.

federal.criterion: The "indication" supporting Column 2 must be the identified, documented clinical rationale for administering the medication, based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

source.quote: INDICATION The identified, documented clinical rationale for administering a medication that is based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

federal.notes: Definition box on the same page as the coding instructions.

federal.criterion: Documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room) should be reviewed.

source.quote: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

federal.notes: Step 2 of Steps for Assessment for N0415.

federal.criterion: Assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the pharmacological classification on the MDS 3.0 (e.g., a consistently used facility resource, the manufacturer's package insert, or the pharmacist).

source.quote: Facilities may wish to identify a resource that their staff consistently use to identify pharmacological classification as assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the MDS 3.0.

federal.notes: Framed as a suggestion ("may wish to") coupled with an expectation that the source can be identified.

federal.criterion: When a resident receives antipsychotic, antianxiety and hypnotic medications simultaneously there must be a clear clinical indication for their use; adequate documentation is essential in justifying their use.

source.quote: Administration of these types of medications, particularly in this combination, could be interpreted as chemically restraining the resident. Adequate documentation is essential in justifying their use.

federal.notes: Stated as a "Please note" following the N0415 coding example.

federal.criterion: Providers are responsible for coding each medication's pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately; the listed external resources are optional and not required for MDS completion.

source.quote: Providers are responsible for coding each medication's pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The N0415 pages (N-4 through N-12) do not tie this item to any payment or case-mix classification.

conflicts.topic: Wording of the look-back window for the Antipsychotic sub-items: "7-day look-back period" vs. "observation period"

positions.claim: N0415A1 is described as covering the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415A1. Antipsychotic: Check if an antipsychotic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

positions.claim: N0415A2 is described as covering "the observation period" without stating 7 days, while the general coding instruction for Column 1 calls it the "7-day observation period."

source.quote: Column 1: Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

conflicts.resolution: Terminology only; the manual uses "7-day look-back period" and "7-day observation period" interchangeably for N0415, and both carry the same "or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days" qualifier.
